steps.title: Import Component, NgModule, and CommonModule
steps.instruction: Import Component and NgModule from '@angular/core', and CommonModule from '@angular/common'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import multiple symbols from each module.
steps.seedCode: // Import Component and NgModule from '@angular/core', and CommonModule from '@angular/common'
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary Angular core modules are imported for creating components and demonstrating context performance.
successCriteria: Component and NgModule are imported from '@angular/core', and CommonModule is imported from '@angular/common'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the required Angular modules. These are essential for creating components and setting up the module structure for our context performance demonstration.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but you need to import all three: Component and NgModule from '@angular/core', and CommonModule from '@angular/common'. Make sure to use the correct import syntax with curly braces.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are not correct. You need to import Component and NgModule from '@angular/core', and CommonModule from '@angular/common'. Check the import statements and try again.

steps.title: Create main AppComponent class with @Component decorator
steps.instruction:
Create the AppComponent class with the @Component decorator. Include selector: 'app-root', template: '

Context Performance Demo

', and styles: [''].
steps.hint: Use the imported Component decorator to define the component metadata.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class is defined with proper Angular component decorator and metadata.
successCriteria: AppComponent class exists with @Component decorator containing selector, template, and styles properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the root AppComponent with the required decorator metadata.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you have all three properties: selector, template, and styles in the @Component decorator.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component definition is incomplete. Check that you have the @Component decorator with selector, template, and styles properties.

steps.title: Initialize performance tracking state variables
steps.instruction: Inside the AppComponent class, add two public properties: renderCount of type number initialized to 0, and lastRenderTime of type number initialized to 0.
steps.hint: Add these properties directly in the class body, using TypeScript type annotations and initial values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class will have two typed number properties to track rendering metrics.
successCriteria: AppComponent has public renderCount: number = 0 and lastRenderTime: number = 0 properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the performance tracking state variables. These will help monitor component renders.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some properties, but make sure both renderCount and lastRenderTime are present with number types and initial values of 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: The properties weren't added correctly. Check that you've declared renderCount: number = 0 and lastRenderTime: number = 0 inside the AppComponent class.

steps.title: Create data array for demonstration
steps.instruction: Inside the AppComponent class, add a property named 'items' of type string[] and initialize it with sample string values like 'Item 1', 'Item 2', etc.
steps.hint: Define a property with type annotation: items: string[] = ['Item 1', 'Item 2', 'Item 3'];
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class now has a 'items' property containing sample string data that will be used for rendering demonstration.
successCriteria: The AppComponent class contains a property named 'items' of type string[] with at least two sample string values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the items array property. This sample data will be used to demonstrate rendering performance.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a property, but check: 1) Is it named 'items'? 2) Does it have type string[]? 3) Is it initialized with sample string values?
steps.feedbackWrong: The items array property is not correctly defined. Make sure to add 'items: string[] = ['Item 1', 'Item 2'];' inside the AppComponent class.

steps.title: Define ngOnInit lifecycle method
steps.instruction: Add the ngOnInit lifecycle method to your AppComponent class to initialize the renderCount and lastRenderTime properties.
steps.hint: Implement the OnInit interface and define ngOnInit() method inside your component class.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class now has an ngOnInit method that will run when the component initializes.
successCriteria: ngOnInit method is defined in AppComponent with proper initialization logic for renderCount and lastRenderTime.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the ngOnInit lifecycle method. This will initialize your performance tracking variables when the component loads.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added ngOnInit, but make sure to initialize both renderCount and lastRenderTime inside the method.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ngOnInit method is not properly defined. Remember to add it inside the AppComponent class and implement the initialization logic.

steps.title: Create updateData handler method
steps.instruction: Inside the AppComponent class, define a method named updateData that modifies the items array and updates the performance tracking variables.
steps.hint: Add a method that pushes a new item to the items array, increments renderCount, and updates lastRenderTime to the current time.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class will have an updateData method that modifies the items array and updates performance metrics.
successCriteria: The updateData method is defined, pushes a new item to the items array, increments renderCount, and updates lastRenderTime.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the updateData method that will modify data and track rendering performance.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a method, but make sure it modifies the items array and updates both renderCount and lastRenderTime.
steps.feedbackWrong: The updateData method is missing or doesn't properly modify the items array and update performance tracking variables.

steps.title: Add performance tracking to ngDoCheck
steps.instruction: Add the ngDoCheck lifecycle method to your AppComponent class to increment renderCount and calculate the time since the last render.
steps.hint: Implement ngDoCheck() to track how often change detection runs. Inside it, increment renderCount and update lastRenderTime with the current timestamp.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent will track each change detection cycle by incrementing renderCount and updating the timing.
successCriteria: ngDoCheck method is implemented, renderCount is incremented, and lastRenderTime is updated with Date.now() inside the method.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented ngDoCheck to track change detection frequency. This will help monitor rendering performance.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added ngDoCheck, but make sure to increment renderCount and update lastRenderTime inside the method.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ngDoCheck method is missing or incomplete. Add the method to track change detection cycles.

steps.title: Create main template structure with header
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent template, replace the existing <h1> with a <header> element containing an <h1> with the title 'Context Performance Demo' and a <div> with the text 'Renders: {{ renderCount }}'.
steps.hint: Update the template property in the @Component decorator to include the header structure.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now has a structured header section displaying the title and the current render count.
successCriteria: The template contains a <header> element with an <h1> and a <div> showing the renderCount using interpolation.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully structured the header with the performance metric display.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the template includes both the <h1> title and the <div> with the render count.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure doesn't match the requirement. Check that you replaced the <h1> with a <header> containing the specified elements.

steps.title: Add data display with *ngFor directive
steps.instruction: In your template, add a <ul> element that uses *ngFor to iterate through the items array and display each item in an <li>.
steps.hint: Use *ngFor="let item of items" on the <li> element to loop through the items array and display each value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: Displaying a list with *ngFor
  • {{ item }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will include a list that dynamically displays each item from the items array using Angular's *ngFor directive.
successCriteria: The template contains a <ul> with an <li> that uses *ngFor="let item of items" and displays {{ item }}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a dynamic list using *ngFor. This demonstrates how Angular can efficiently render collections.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have both the <ul> and <li> elements, and that the *ngFor directive is correctly placed on the <li> with the syntax "let item of items".
steps.feedbackWrong: The list isn't displaying correctly. Check that you've added the <ul> and <li> elements and used the *ngFor directive properly to iterate through the items array.

steps.title: Add update button and wire click event
steps.instruction: Add a button element to the template with a (click) event binding that calls the updateData() method. Place it after the existing header.
steps.hint: Use the Angular event binding syntax (click)="updateData()" on a <button> element.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click event
<button (click)="handleClick()">Update Items</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will include a button that triggers data updates when clicked, enabling interactive performance observation.
successCriteria: A button element with (click)="updateData()" is added to the template after the header.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added an interactive button that will trigger data updates and allow you to observe performance changes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but make sure it has the correct event binding (click)="updateData()" to call the updateData method.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button with the proper click event binding wasn't found. Add a <button> element with (click)="updateData()" to the template.
